summary: Attempted to extend the sweep with configuration events aimed at an existing serving member (so a voter could be demoted and re-promoted) and it failed in a way worth keeping rather than hiding. With application lag present, aiming a JointImplicit change at a serving member made the harness panic with 'config is already joint' inside applyConfChange: a node applies a joint-entering change while its own tracked configuration is still joint, because the leave-joint entry that should precede it is exactly what the lag event holds back. That is the target's documented treatment of an invalid configuration change, so the failure is a harness modelling error - it applied a change out of the order the contract assumes at that node - not a target defect. I reverted to the last known-good revision (configuration events on the joining node 4 only, JointImplicit half the time, application lag, restarts, the liveness witness) and confirmed locally that it runs again and reproduces the executed counters exactly (elections=470, ordinary proposals=461, conf_change_proposals=262, restarts=429, unapplied_conf_change_states=48, stalled_states=0, violations=0), so no experiment was requested. The failure did open a real sourced follow-up, registered as investigation @joint_apply_order: with Config.DisableConfChangeValidation at its default the leader's propose-time check is explicitly best-effort against a possibly stale configuration with both false positives and false negatives, so a joint-entering change can be appended while some lagging node is still joint; the question is whether a permitted history can force a node to apply a committed change while joint, what the target requires of the application (log-order application, or something stronger about proposals in flight during a joint configuration), and whether the panic is bounded by application duties alone or by anything the target enforces - with a discriminator that withholds one follower's application while a second joint change is proposed, and a control where the follower keeps up.
